task.title: Transactional UTF-8 line importer
task.specification: config={maxBytes:integer 8..256}. Events are {type:'chunk',bytes:[integers 0..255]} or {type:'finish'}. Buffer bytes until LF byte 10; LF is not part of the frame or buffer limit. Each complete frame must be valid strict UTF-8 and JSON. Frames have exact schemas: {op:'begin',id:string}, {op:'put',key:string,value:JSON scalar}, {op:'commit',id:string}, {op:'abort'}. Begin is legal only with no open transaction; put only with an open transaction; commit only for its ID; abort is always legal. A transaction stages puts over current visible data and commit publishes all of them atomically. Any invalid frame increments errors once and abandons the open transaction. Once a line exceeds maxBytes, count one error, abandon the transaction, and discard bytes through its next LF without another error. Finish counts one error for a nonempty partial line (but no extra error for an already-overflowed line), then clears it; if a transaction is still open, count one further error and abandon it. Finish is not a permanent shutdown. Output {visible,open,buffered,errors}, open is ID or null and buffered counts retained frame bytes. Blank lines are invalid frames; escaped newlines in JSON strings are data. Return one JSON output per event; state is opaque JSON, initially null. Objects in outputs have exactly the documented keys; map keys are unordered, arrays are ordered. Sorted/lexicographic string order compares Unicode scalar values (code points), with a shorter prefix first. Numeric inputs/values and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number notations such as 1 and 1.0 denote the same number, while booleans are distinct. Strings contain Unicode scalar values (no unpaired surrogates). Decoded imported values outside these limits are invalid frames. There are at most 48 events. Unknown/invalid operations have the behavior below. Each instance starts fresh. Hidden ordinary cases vary legal values; boundary cases emphasize equality, empty data and duplicates; adversarial cases reorder and conflict; shift cases use longer traces and more identities within the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Cartographic generalization
matchedCard.relation: At a smaller representation scale, selection, simplification, and combination can preserve legibility while omitting detail. The resulting representation depends on scale and purpose; omission from that representation does not establish absence from the represented world.
assumptions: The representation has a specified scale and communicative purpose.
A more detailed source contains distinctions from which the representation is derived.
matchedCard.boundary: Simplification can remove a distinction important for another purpose. A reduced representation cannot recover information that it does not encode.
matchedCard.source_fact: USGS describes cartographic generalization as selecting and reducing detail to produce representations appropriate to scale.

shuffledCard.label: Lighthouse sector signals
shuffledCard.relation: A navigational source can provide a general identifying signal and a separate directional indication for a particular hazard. What a sector indication signifies depends on the observer's position and its relationship to the marked region.
assumptions: The source and the meaning of its sector can be identified.
The observer has sufficient visibility and positional context to interpret the indication.
shuffledCard.boundary: A sector signal describes only its designated region. An ordinary indication does not certify that every nearby route is hazard-free, and poor visibility can limit interpretation.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Trinity House describes Start Point's white navigational flashes and a separate red sector marking the shallow Skerries Bank, alongside a low-visibility hazard warning signal.

sources.title: Trinity House completes re-engineering of Start Point Lighthouse

initial.explanation: Use a conditional invariant: retained buffered bytes are exactly the current unterminated line, excluding LF and excluding discarded overflow bytes. Complete lines are decoded and validated before transactional state changes; invalid lines increment errors and clear the open transaction.
initial.mapping: The rule maps each event to buffered length, while open, visible, and errors are updated only by validated frames, overflow, or finish recovery.
initial.assumptions: Inputs obey the public event and config domains. JSON frame objects must have exactly the documented keys; imported values are scalar and safe.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;let b=0,d=false,m=input.config.maxBytes;for(let i=0;i<output.length;i++){let e=input.events[i];if(e.type==='chunk'){for(let x of e.bytes){if(d){if(x===10)d=false}else if(x===10)b=0;else if(++b>m){b=0;d=true}}}else if(e.type==='finish'){b=0;d=false}if(output[i].buffered!==b)return false}return true}

final.explanation: Retains only the current unterminated line, discarding an overflowed line through its next LF. Complete lines are strictly UTF-8/JSON validated against the exact operation schemas; invalid frames, overflow, and finish recovery abandon transactions as specified. Transactional puts remain staged until a matching commit, which atomically publishes them.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{v:{},o:null,t:{},b:[],d:false,e:0},M=config.maxBytes;const drop=()=>{s.e++;s.o=null;s.t={}};function str(x){return typeof x==='string'&&!/[\ud800-\udfff]/.test(x)}function scalar(x){return x===null||typeof x==='boolean'||str(x)||(typeof x==='number'&&Number.isSafeInteger(x))}function dec(a){let z='',i=0;while(i<a.length){let c=a[i++],n,u;if(c<128){u=c;n=0}else if(c>=194&&c<=223){u=c&31;n=1}else if(c>=224&&c<=239){u=c&15;n=2}else if(c>=240&&c<=244){u=c&7;n=3}else return null;if(i+n>a.length)return null;for(let j=0;j<n;j++){let q=a[i++];if((q&192)!==128)return null;u=u*64+(q&63)}if(n===2&&(u<2048||u>=55296&&u<=57343)||n===3&&(u<65536||u>1114111))return null;z+=String.fromCodePoint(u)}return z}function parse(a){let q=dec(a),x,k;if(q===null)return null;try{x=JSON.parse(q)}catch(_){return null}if(!x||Array.isArray(x)||typeof x!=='object'||typeof x.op!=='string')return null;k=Object.keys(x);if(x.op==='begin')return k.length===2&&str(x.id)?x:null;if(x.op==='put')return k.length===3&&str(x.key)&&scalar(x.value)?x:null;if(x.op==='commit')return k.length===2&&str(x.id)?x:null;if(x.op==='abort')return k.length===1?x:null;return null}function line(){let x=parse(s.b);s.b=[];if(!x){drop();return}if(x.op==='begin'){if(s.o!==null)drop();else{s.o=x.id;s.t={}}}else if(x.op==='put'){if(s.o===null)drop();else s.t[x.key]=x.value}else if(x.op==='commit'){if(s.o===null||s.o!==x.id)drop();else{for(let k of Object.keys(s.t))s.v[k]=s.t[k];s.o=null;s.t={}}}else{s.o=null;s.t={}}}if(event.type==='chunk')for(let x of event.bytes){if(s.d){if(x===10)s.d=false;continue}if(x===10)line();else if(s.b.length<M)s.b.push(x);else{s.b=[];s.d=true;drop()}}else{if(!s.d&&s.b.length){s.e++;s.b=[];s.o=null;s.t={}}else{s.b=[];s.d=false}if(s.o!==null)drop()}return{state:s,output:{visible:s.v,open:s.o,buffered:s.b.length,errors:s.e}}}

initial.explanation: The rule is: retained bytes are counted exactly, while LF terminates and removes a frame. Invalid frames or overflow abandon transactions, and valid transactional operations update staged or visible data according to the protocol.
initial.mapping: The rule maps line-buffer retention to buffered, transaction visibility to open/visible, and recovery events to errors.
initial.assumptions: JSON.parse with fatal UTF-8 decoding is available. JSON objects used as maps have ordinary string keys; decoded scalar numbers must be safe integers.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(const x of output){if(!x||typeof x!=="object"||!Number.isInteger(x.buffered)||!Number.isInteger(x.errors)||!((x.open===null)||typeof x.open==='string')||!x.visible||typeof x.visible!=="object")return false}let b=0;for(const q of input.events){if(q.type==='chunk'){for(const n of q.bytes){if(n===10){b=0;break}b++}}else if(q.type==='finish')b=0}return output.length?output[0].buffered===((input.events[0].type==='chunk')?(()=>{let n=0;for(const b of input.events[0].bytes){if(b===10)break;n++}return n})():0):true}

final.explanation: Retains bytes only until LF, enforces overflow recovery, validates UTF-8 and JSON frames, stages transactional updates, and reports visible data, transaction state, buffered bytes, and cumulative errors after every event.

initial.explanation: The implementation treats each LF-delimited byte sequence as one frame, enforces strict UTF-8 and JSON validation, stages transaction changes, and recovers from malformed or oversized input exactly once per failure.
initial.mapping: The state maps visible data, open transaction ID, staged values, retained bytes, overflow mode, and error count. Each event produces the documented projection.
initial.assumptions: JSON numbers must be safe integers; put values are JSON scalars. Objects must have exactly the required fields and no extra fields.
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){const M=config.maxBytes;let s=state||{v:{},o:null,t:{},b:[],x:0,e:0};const bad=()=>{s.e++;s.o=null;s.t={}};const utf=a=>{let r='';for(let i=0;i<a.length;i++){let c=a[i];if(c<128)r+=String.fromCharCode(c);else{let n=c<224?1:c<240?2:3;if(i+n>=a.length)return null;let z=0;if(n==1){if(c<194)return null;z=c&31}else if(n==2){if((a[i+1]&192)!=128)return null;z=(c&15)<<6|a[++i]&63}else{if((a[i+1]&192)!=128||(a[i+2]&192)!=128)return null;z=(c&7)<<12|(a[++i]&63)<<6|a[++i]&63}if(z>=55296&&z<=57343||z>1114111)return null;r+=String.fromCodePoint(z)}}return r};const scalar=x=>x===null||typeof x==='string'||typeof x==='boolean'||typeof x==='number'&&Number.isSafeInteger(x);const frame=a=>{if(!a.length){bad();return}let q=utf(a),o;try{o=JSON.parse(q)}catch(e){bad();return}if(!q||q[0]!=='{'||!o||Array.isArray(o)||typeof o!=='object'){bad();return}let k=Object.keys(o),op=o.op;if(op==='begin'&&k.length===2&&k.includes('id')&&typeof o.id==='string'&&s.o===null){s.o=o.id;s.t={};return}if(op==='put'&&k.length===3&&k.includes('key')&&k.includes('value')&&typeof o.key==='string'&&scalar(o.value)&&s.o!==null){s.t[o.key]=o.value;return}if(op==='commit'&&k.length===2&&k.includes('id')&&typeof o.id==='string'&&s.o===o.id){for(let z in s.t)s.v[z]=s.t[z];s.o=null;s.t={};return}if(op==='abort'&&k.length===1){s.o=null;s.t={};return}bad()};const line=()=>{if(s.x){s.x=0;s.b=[];return}frame(s.b);s.b=[]};if(event.type==='chunk'){for(let c of event.bytes){if(s.x){if(c===10)line();continue}if(c===10){line();continue}s.b.push(c);if(s.b.length>M){s.e++;s.o=null;s.t={};s.x=1;s.b=[]}}}else if(event.type==='finish'){if(s.b.length){s.e++;s.b=[]}else if(s.x){s.x=0}if(s.o!==null){s.e++;s.o=null;s.t={}}}return{state:s,output:{visible:s.v,open:s.o,buffered:s.b.length,errors:s.e}}}
